neighbours.label: The word ' so' used as a connector joining two clauses, for result or purpose, with or without a comma ('the pipes froze so the street lost water', 'he labelled the boxes so nothing got lost', 'it starts at nine, so bring a laptop'). Quiet for 'so' meaning 'very' after is/was/felt ('the soup was so hot'), for fixed phrases ('if so', 'or so', 'I think so', 'and so on', 'even so', 'so-called'), and for the same link made without 'so' ('therefore', 'because', 'in order to').
neighbours.short: ' so' joining two clauses (result or purpose)
fire: The pipes froze overnight so the whole street lost water.
He labelled every box so nothing got lost during the move.
The meeting starts at nine, so bring your laptop.
It was raining hard, so we stayed inside and played cards.
She saved a little each month so she could visit her sister in spring.
The bridge was closed for repairs, so drivers took the long way around.
Speak a bit louder so the people in the back can hear you.
The battery was almost dead so I plugged in the phone.
quiet: The pipes froze overnight and therefore the whole street lost water.
He labelled every box in order to keep track of everything during the move.
The soup was so hot that nobody could eat it yet.
Will the meeting start at nine? If so, I'll bring my laptop.
We waited for an hour or so before the bus finally came.
She felt so tired after the long shift at the hospital.
Is it going to rain tomorrow? I think so.
The shop sells pens, paper, folders and so on.
